title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. π is the fundamental group of a surface or orbifold Π. It is realised as the automorphism group of a fixed universal covering Π̃, so the groupoid ⟨π⟩ (one object, automorphism group π) is identified with the groupoid of universal coverings of Π. A group Σ acts on π by outer automorphisms; this is what Grothendieck calls an 'orientation of Σ' on the data. Natural candidates for Σ are a Galois group or a mapping class / symmetry group.

Previous page. A π-set T, with Σ acting compatibly, yields the transport (action) groupoid ⟨T,π⟩. In it, Isom(t,t') = π_{t,t'} = {λ ∈ π : λt = t'}. There is a canonical faithful functor ⟨T,π⟩ → ⟨π⟩ that forgets the objects and includes each π_{t,t'} into π.

This page ('Inversement'). Grothendieck tries to characterise such data intrinsically. He starts from:
- a groupoid Λ (a 'T-groupoïde'), with object set C = Ob Λ a Σ-set;
- a Σ-action on (T,Λ);
- a faithful functor f: Λ → ⟨π⟩, compatible with the Σ-actions.

Concretely, f is a family of injections Isom_Λ(t,t') ↪ π, with image π_{t,t'}, compatible with composition. He notes in brackets that such a faithful functor amounts to two pieces of data:
- a family of subgroups (π_t)_{t∈C} of π (the images of Aut_Λ(t));
- 'bitransporter' sets π_{t,t'}, which are a (π_{t'}, π_t)-bitorsor inside π.
The page breaks off with 'we will now introduce the operations…'.

Next page. The missing condition is supplied. For each t, the sets π_{t,t'} (t' varying) must form a partition of π. In other words, every λ ∈ π has a unique lift to an arrow of Λ with source t. This says f is a covering morphism of groupoids (a discrete fibration). That condition gives an action of π on Ob Λ and an isomorphism Λ ≅ ⟨T,π⟩ over ⟨π⟩. The further hypothesis that the stabilisers π_t are pairwise distinct then gives a family of groups indexed by the orbits T/π, with Σ acting compatibly.

What it serves. This is a base-point-free, Σ-equivariant (outer-action) encoding of a π-set together with its stabilisers. The typical example is the set of cusps or boundary components of a surface, with their inertia subgroups, in the Teichmüller / Galois setting of 'Paradigmes'. Grothendieck himself comments on the next page 'Ce n'est pas bien éclairant' ('this is not very illuminating') and looks for another approach.
errors: As stated on this page, a faithful functor Λ → ⟨π⟩ alone does not make Λ an action groupoid ⟨T,π⟩: faithfulness only gives the subgroups π_t and bitorsors π_{t,t'}. The unique-lifting (covering) condition is needed, and Grothendieck supplies it only on the next page. The page is a draft, not an error as such.

The 'Σ-orientation' compatibility is stated loosely. Since Σ acts on π only by outer automorphisms, compatibility of f with Σ must be understood up to inner automorphisms, i.e. as an action on the groupoid of universal covers. This is not made precise here.

ideas.what: Action/transport groupoid ⟨T,π⟩ with Isom(t,t') = {λ : λt = t'}, and the forgetful faithful functor to the one-object groupoid ⟨π⟩
ideas.modern_name: action groupoid T//π; forgetful functor to Bπ
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (fundamental groupoid, fibred categories); Pursuing Stacks uses such groupoids

ideas.what: Faithful functor from a groupoid into ⟨π⟩ described by subgroups π_t and bitransporter (bitorsor) subsets π_{t,t'}
ideas.modern_name: faithful functors into BG / subgroupoid data

ideas.what: Recovering a π-set from a groupoid over ⟨π⟩ via unique lifting of arrows (worked out on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: covering morphisms of groupoids ≃ π-sets (discrete fibrations over Bπ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown, P. J. Higgins; Grothendieck's fibred categories (SGA1)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V–VI (Galois categories, fibred categories)

ideas.what: Outer action of Σ realised as an action on the groupoid of universal covers (base-point-free), applied to cusp/inertia data
ideas.modern_name: outer Galois/mapping-class actions on fundamental groupoids with several base points (tangential base points)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (fundamental groupoids with suitably chosen base points)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine groupoid bookkeeping: action groupoids and the correspondence between covering morphisms and π-sets, in an outer-action setting. Grothendieck himself judges it 'not very illuminating'. It fits the known Esquisse-era programme of base-point-free fundamental groupoids with Galois/Teichmüller actions. There is nothing that would be new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The final line most likely reads 'On va maintenant introduire les op. de' (continuing as 'π sur Λ' on the next page), not 'les q. des'.
'On exprime la donnée' is probably 'Ceci exprime la donnée' or 'Cela exprime la donnée d'un foncteur fidèle d'un groupoïde Λ dans ⟨π⟩'.

The marginal gloss near the arrow f reads 'foncteur fidèle'. The target is described as 'groupoïde des revêtements universels de Π' (rendered 'un seul type' in the transcription; uncertain), equivalent to ⟨π⟩ via a chosen Π̃ 'dont les autos sont π'.
The underbraced label π_{t,t'} sits under 'Isom_Λ(t,t') ↪ π', i.e. it names the image subset of the injection.
The bracket '[dans C est un Σ ens.]' is probably '[où C est un Σ-ensemble]'.
